findings.description: The woman carries a clearly red bag at her side from 0.0s to 2.0s. At 2.25s the object in her hand has turned pale pink and faint, and by 2.5-2.75s it is gone entirely, although her hands are visible and neither the phone nor anything else blocks them.

The on-screen UI is nonsensical AI-style text: the main readout 'A7·42' has a stray macron over the A, the header reads 'A‾A', and there are meaningless 'x2' and 'AZ-12' labels and scattered stray marks. The glyphs also change shape over the clip: early frames read like '3742'/'λ742' with no dot, later ones read 'A7·42', and at 9.25s it reads 'A·4X'. A real display would not do this.

A large bright glare patch with a blocky shadow edge jumps position on the screen from frame to frame and switches on and off while the phone and hands barely move. It is present at 6.5s, gone at 6.75s, back at 7.0s, gone at 7.25s and back at 8.0s. The flicker has no plausible light source or occluder, and it washes out and restores the digits beneath it.
